cases.notes: Without a confirming separator line this remains paragraph text.
Exact-cell < is ordinary table content; table spans are Grid-only in 0.1.0.
Exact-cell ^ is ordinary table content; table spans are Grid-only in 0.1.0.
Sequences resembling Grid continuation geometry remain ordinary table-cell content.
^ and < have no table-span semantics; inline code also preserves them literally.
A first-body-row ^ cell is valid ordinary content because tables have no rowspan semantics.
A first-column < cell is valid ordinary content because tables have no colspan semantics.
Table cells do not resolve span geometry; this is an ordinary rectangular 3-column table.
A row of ^ cells is ordinary table content, not a row covered by spans.
The first line is claimed by list structure before table confirmation. The following baseline line is a separate block, not a retroactive table separator.
Tables participate in the document-wide durable block-ID relation.
The line-2 separator confirms the table (§12.3); its lower cell count than the header is a syntax error, not a paragraph fallback.
A separator cell count exceeding the header is a §12.3 syntax error.
